author: Brenn Allen Flores
title: 'I was pretending to be a coach': JJ Redick makes blunt admission about coaching the Lakers - NewsBreak
text:
By Brenn Allen Flores ,
7 hours ago Image by Keith Allisonderivative work: Chrishmt0423, CC BY-SA 3.0. Via Wikimedia Commons. Entering his third season as head coach of the Los Angeles Lakers, JJ Redick offered an honest self-assessment regarding his early transition from the broadcast booth to the NBA sidelines, admitting he initially felt like he was playing a role rather than authentically leading the team. Speaking to reporters during Lakers training camp, the 42-year-old coach reflected on how experience and summer reflection have reshaped his approach heading into the 2026-27 campaign.
According to EssentiallySports , Redick noted that gaining daily repetitions helped establish the necessary comfort level to manage players and execute detailed game plans effectively. “As I reflected this summer, probably shouldn’t admit this, but early in my coaching career, it felt like I was cosplaying a little bit,” he said. “And I was like I was pretending to be a coach. And I just think you get more reps, you get more comfortable. I don’t think the confidence was ever not there, and you also just know what you want.”
Redick also revealed that conversations with his former Duke head coach Mike Krzyzewski during the offseason altered his emotional demeanor on the bench. The long-time NBA guard explained that the inner fury that fueled his 15-year playing career proved counterproductive when leading a team.
Redick Is Entering A New Era Of Lakers Basketball “Some of the things that helped me as a player are deterrents for me as a coach,” Redick stated. “When I played, I played with an anger. There was an inner anger that drove my competitiveness. That’s not always a good thing as a coach, particularly now. I felt like calm is better.”
Following the departure of LeBron James to the Philadelphia 76ers, the Lakers front office pivoted by constructing the roster around point guard Luka Doncic, guard Austin Reaves, and center Walker Kessler. The roster overhaul added Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams alongside Quentin Grimes. This upcoming season marks the first time Redick will not coach James on the Lakers .
Redick guided Los Angeles to 50 regular-season wins in his inaugural year and followed with 53 victories last season, but both postseason trips ended with early playoff exits. With new personnel suited for a faster early offense and structured team defense, Redick outlined three distinct priorities for the current camp session: strengthening defensive principles, pushing transition offense, and conditioning.
“I have three goals for camp,” JJ Redick said regarding his daily expectations. “Continue to establish our defensive principles. Continue to establish our early offense, which has been our main priority for all of September. And then lastly, just get in great shape.”
With starting positions around Doncic, Reaves, and Kessler still up for grabs, Redick emphasized that rotation decisions will be based strictly on performance during practice scrimmages rather than past credentials. Los Angeles will open their preseason against the Sacramento Kings on Monday.
